newsitem.title: GERMANY: Survey shows smaller German companies against EMU.
newsitem.headline: Survey shows smaller German companies against EMU.

text.p: A majority of small and mid-sized firms in Germany are against European currency union, saying it would have a negative impact on their operations, according to a survey by DG Bank released on Wednesday.
But the survey of about 2,500 businesses also showed that companies with foreign operations, and also those who have learned about currency union, had lower fears than others.
"The worries seem to subside for those who are better informed and also those who have more experience with foreign operations," DG Bank chief economist Michael Heise said.

The survey also showed concerns about German employment once currency union starts in January 1999, with 40 percent of those in the survey saying they expected the euro to cut jobs and only 15 percent saying it may create new jobs.
About 40 percent of the companies in the survey saw the new currency helping Germany but some 35 percent said it would have a rather negative impact, DG Bank said.
